 MAGA pundit 'regrets' Trump's behavior after epic loss: He has 'whiff of corruption'
 By:
 Matthew Chapman
 Nov 19, 2026
 7:04AM ET
 Matthew Chapman
 Matthew Chapman attended Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and lives in San Marcos, Texas. Before joining Raw Story, he wrote for Shareblue and AlterNet, specializing in election and policy coverage.
 SEE FULL BIO
 Make us preferred on Google Comments 0 Share Article
 Conservative pundit Ben Shapiro said he regretted how President Donald Trump performed — but not his vote.
 In an interview with NPR’s Steve Inskeep on “Newsmakers,” Shapiro said, “I don’t regret my vote.” Shapiro voted against Trump in 2016 but stumped for his campaign in 2024. Now, he says, he is disappointed by the president’s tariffs, alleged corruption, and handling of the Iran war.
 Shapiro said a general “whiff of corruption” around the White House , specifically the Trump family’s crypto company World Liberty Financial , aggressive immigration enforcement, and other issues contributed to Republican midterm losses, NPR reported.
 He also said Republicans faced difficult prospects in 2028 and that Vice President JD Vance wasn’t the ideal nominee. Speaking to Inskeep, Shapiro argued Vance would shrink the 2024 Trump coalition of Hispanic, working-class, women, and college-educated voters. Shapiro said Vance was “extraordinarily online” and "militantly, militantly antiestablishment in ways that are designed to appeal to 21-year-old Joe Rogan listeners."
 He pointed to Secretary of State Marco Rubio as a candidate with broader appeal, though he said many in the White House would likely be harmed by their association with the current administration.
 Shapiro, co-founder of The Daily Wire, said he had stayed consistent in his beliefs, and went after a number of his fellow far-right MAGA pundits, calling Megyn Kelly a “weather vane,” criticizing Tucker Carlson over claims that Israel controls the United States, and all but calling the latter's remarks antisemitic. NPR wrote that Carlson denied expressing antisemitic views when he appeared on “Newsmakers” in September.
 NPR wrote that Shapiro also discussed his new movie, “Confession,” and the decline in his show’s YouTube subscriptions.
